name: Il Platano di Piazza Sant'Ambrogio

location.address: Piazza Sant'Ambrogio / Largo Caduti Milanesi per la Patria, 20123 Milano

verified_sources: MASAF national register, sheet 52/F205/MI/03, Milano, Piazza Sant'Ambrogio - Largo Caduti Milanesi per La Patria (Platanus acerifolia, girth 420 cm, height 34 m)

https://www.lombardiaspeciale.regione.lombardia.it/wps/portal/LS/?urile=wcm:path:/lspeciale/news/2025/11-+novembre/nws-lombardia-alberi-monumentali/nws-lombardia-alberi-monumentali (Regione Lombardia press page, 18 Nov 2025, naming this plane among 48 new entries to the national monumental-tree list, alongside the Viale Cervantes plane and the Brera ginkgo group)
access: Free, public square outside the Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio
verify_notes: Two independent sources: the MASAF national register (tree-level coordinate, girth 420 cm, height 34 m) and Regione Lombardia's own 18 Nov 2025 press announcement, which names this exact plane (grouped with Largo Caduti Milanesi per la Patria, the square's other name, not a second tree; register locality string confirms it is one entry, sheet_id 52/F205/MI/03) as one of 48 trees newly added to the national Elenco alberi monumentali, bringing Lombardy to 476 recognised specimens. The Nov 2025 designation date itself is good alive-now evidence, nine months old. No age published anywhere; range is a girth-based estimate matching similarly-sized planes elsewhere in the city (mil_012 at 483 cm girth carries the same 100-180 range). Stands on the square in front of the Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio (founded 379 AD, current building 11th-12th century), technically basilica/Universita Cattolica-adjacent ground rather than a municipal park, but it is a public square with open access. Distance note for the writer: 1.2 km / roughly 15 min walk from the Parco Sempione cluster (mil_010, and mil_017 below), on the way toward the historic centre; does not sit inside an existing walk but is close enough that a 'centre to Sempione' route could plausibly link them. Not on the comune's list of 13 published monumental-tree pages (comune.milano.it is currently blocking all fetches, 403 on both curl and WebFetch, so that source could not be rechecked this pass). Species per hard rule 9: Platanus x acerifolia is canonically 'London Plane'.

name: Il Platano di Viale Cervantes
verified_sources: MASAF national register, sheet 53/F205/MI/03, Milano, Viale Cervantes - Parco Sempione (Platanus acerifolia, girth 390 cm, height 33 m)

https://www.lombardiaspeciale.regione.lombardia.it/wps/portal/LS/?urile=wcm:path:/lspeciale/news/2025/11-+novembre/nws-lombardia-alberi-monumentali/nws-lombardia-alberi-monumentali (Regione Lombardia press page, 18 Nov 2025, naming this plane among the same batch of 48 new entries)
access: Free, public park (Parco Sempione, opening hours vary by season)
transport: 8 min walk from Cadorna (M1/M2) or Arco della Pace tram stop
verify_notes: Two independent sources: MASAF register (tree-level coordinate, girth 390 cm, height 33 m) and Regione Lombardia's 18 Nov 2025 announcement naming this plane specifically at Viale Cervantes / Parco Sempione as a new national-register entry, in the same batch as mil_016. Nov 2025 designation date is recent alive-now evidence. No age published; range estimated from girth against comparable planes. This is the second monumental tree in Parco Sempione alongside mil_010 (the Caucasian wingnut, also on Viale Cervantes), so it extends that cluster rather than opening a new one; the two are close enough to visit together (same avenue). A previous pass (data/leads/milan.json) held this back as single-sourced ('the smallest registered plane in central Milan'); the Regione Lombardia press page is the second source that was missing. Species per hard rule 9: 'London Plane'. NOTE: a third possible candidate at this cluster, a 40 m Himalayan Cedar at Viale Cervantes reported by the crowd-sourced site ilregistrodeglialberi.it (RAMI) with an October 2021 survey (girth 380 cm, health 'Buona'), is NOT included here: RAMI is a collaborative/citizen platform, not a government register, and no second source was found for it this pass. Worth a dedicated look next time; if real, a 40 m cedar would be a striking addition to the Sempione cluster.

name: Il Platano dei 34 Metri ai Giardini Montanelli

location.address: Giardini Pubblici Indro Montanelli, Via Palestro, 20121 Milano

verified_sources: MASAF national register, sheet 11/F205/MI/03, Giardini Indro Montanelli - Corso Venezia (Platanus acerifolia, girth 475 cm, height 34 m)

https://www.ilgiorno.it/milano/cronaca/alberi-monumentali-1.7590565 (Il Giorno, 'Verde, sono 17 gli alberi monumentali a Milano', quoting verbatim: 'un altro platano, anche in questo caso ai Giardini Montanelli di via Palestro' reaching the same 34-metre height as the Villa Litta plane, described as the tallest plant height in the city)
access: Free, public park (opening hours vary by season)
transport: 5 min walk from Palestro (M1) or Porta Venezia (M1)
verify_notes: Two independent sources: MASAF register (tree-level coordinate, girth 475 cm, height 34 m) gives this the joint-tallest plant height in Milan per Il Giorno's own framing, tied with the Villa Litta plane (mil_015's cluster). Il Giorno's newspaper survey independently confirms a second, distinct plane at Giardini Montanelli reaching 34 m, on via Palestro, separate from the garden's more famous 830 cm/24 m plane (mil_002, dated 239 years by the same article) and from mil_012 (483 cm/32 m). No age given by either source; range is a girth-based estimate. This is the fifth register-listed plane in the Giardini Montanelli alongside mil_002, mil_012 and two more (mil_003 is a hackberry, mil_001 a bald cypress, mil_013 a wingnut); it extends the existing five-tree Montanelli cluster to six candidates. A companion register row 200 m away (sheet 03/F205/MI/03, 625 cm girth, 28 m, at 45.473889/9.200833) remains single-sourced (MASAF only, comune.milano.it now blocked to fetches) and is left in leads rather than delivered. BONUS finding for the writer/curator, not acted on here: Il Giorno's verbatim text gives the Villa Litta plane (mil_015's cluster) an age of 176 years and a height of 34 m, which conflicts with the MASAF register's tallest Villa Litta entry (550 cm girth / 43 m, the figure mil_015's story currently uses as 'the tallest registered tree in Milan'). The newspaper's 34 m/176-year tree and the register's 43 m tree may not be the same specimen among Villa Litta's four register rows; worth resolving before quoting either figure with confidence. Species per hard rule 9: 'London Plane'.
